analysis.title: FX Daily Snapshot: USD weakens alongside continued move lower in energy prices
key_insights: The dollar index fell to an overnight low of 101.54, below Friday's high of 102.36, after giving back all of its gains from the stronger NFP report on Friday.

Brent has fallen back towards USD90/barrel for the first time since the end of August and is down about 23% this month, the sharpest sell-off since May-June. The Norwegian krone was the worst performing G10 currency in that earlier period and has again underperformed this month.

The energy decline is driven by renewed optimism over a US-Iran deal after the US mid-term elections. President Trump said "Iran, militarily, is effectively over" and met Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani.

The 10-year US Treasury yield has fallen 50bps from last month's high of 5.36%. Further progress toward a US-Iran deal would help sustain lower energy prices and ease pressure on the Fed and other major central banks to keep hiking.
US October CPI is the main focus today. Core inflation has surprised to the upside for two consecutive months, and consensus expects the monthly change in core CPI to slow to 0.2% from 0.3%.

The rate market still expects the Fed to hike again in December and has scaled back expectations for 2027 to one additional hike. The December hike was more fully priced back in after Friday's stronger NFP and the overnight rebound in AI-related and tech stocks.
The Nasdaq composite rebounded 2.7% and closed back above support from its 200-day moving average at around 25,107.

The euro is in a relief rally on lower energy prices. Leveraged funds are heavily short the euro, with positions at the highest level since early 2020, which leaves it vulnerable to a short squeeze if concerns over the energy shock keep fading.

The 10-year French-German yield spread has narrowed to around 145bps from a high of around 175bps in October. MUFG attributes this to positive external developments, not French fiscal policy. The Swiss franc underperformed yesterday as French fiscal risk eased and AI-related stocks rebounded.

risk_factors: A hot US October core CPI print would add to evidence of broadening inflation beyond energy and reinforce Fed tightening.
Stalled progress on a US-Iran deal would reverse the fall in energy prices and renew pressure on the euro, French spreads and global yields.
French fiscal risk remains a driver of euro area borrowing costs and euro selling pressure.
A rebound in AI-related stocks has boosted the case for a December Fed hike.
vol_and_positioning: IMM positioning shows leveraged funds heavily short the euro, with shorts rising sharply since mid-September to the highest level since the start of the COVID shock in early 2020. MUFG flags short squeeze risk for the euro.
The Nasdaq composite closed back above its 200-day moving average support at around 25,107 after a 2.7% rebound.
geopolitical: Renewed optimism over progress toward a US-Iran deal following the US mid-term elections.

President Trump told reporters that "Iran, militarily, is effectively over" after meeting Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, who said he was grateful for positive discussions on reaching a deal and bringing peace to the region.
